drafts.rationale: The constitution states Foundry's purpose is to convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: The founding thesis states that implementation artifacts are replaceable while decisions are durable, and that the durable asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, contracts, invariants, rationale, authority, and verification obligations.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 1 states that no artifact is canonical merely because it exists; existing code, tests, runtime behavior, and human statements may be evidence, but existence does not automatically create authority, and a production behavior can be real and still wrong.
drafts.subject: Artifacts

drafts.rationale: Law 2 requires Foundry to continuously reason about intended state versus actual state and requires every operation to help explain, reduce, verify, or explicitly authorize that delta, across greenfield, brownfield, incidents, and autonomous maintenance.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 3 states that no model is the canonical memory of a project, persistent state lives outside models, and context is rented only for the minimum sufficient to the current job. The v2 design restates this as bounded compiled inputs and identity that survives model replacement.
drafts.subject: Models

drafts.rationale: Law 4 requires routing work to the cheapest mechanism that can reliably satisfy the required confidence, risk, and verification level, in the order deterministic computation, cheap model, stronger model, frontier reasoning, then human authority. v2 section 20 applies that order to retrieval, routine relations, high-risk merges, and human escalation.
drafts.subject: Foundry work routing

drafts.rationale: Law 5 forbids the process that creates a proposal or artifact from being its sole authority for correctness and separates generation from verification. v2 restates this as refused transitions when two AI judges disagree and human authority for unresolved high-authority semantic conflict.
drafts.subject: Generation

drafts.rationale: Law 6 treats materially ambiguous intent as a first-class defect, requires increasing specification precision only as far as required, and requires distinguishing a missing decision from an ambiguous decision and from one that exceeds a worker's reasoning capability.
drafts.subject: Intent

drafts.rationale: Law 7 requires every material belief to distinguish confidence, authority, and provenance, and states that a highly confident inference is still an inference unless authorized as canonical intent. v2 preserves this by placing confidence on judgments and authority on claims.
drafts.subject: Material beliefs

drafts.rationale: Law 8 states research cannot directly mutate canonical intent and must follow Research to Evidence to Reasoning to Authorization to Canonical State, preserving provenance, disagreement, and uncertainty. v2 makes that flow structural by recording judgments separately from applied state transitions.
drafts.subject: Research

drafts.rationale: Law 9 requires every material unknown to be resolved or explicitly controlled, and an uncontrolled material unknown must block affected downstream work. v2 restates this by keeping disputed conflicts in durable state unconditionally.
drafts.subject: Material unknowns

drafts.rationale: Law 10 requires an append-only history of material events, claims, evidence, decisions, verification outcomes, and promotions so current state is reconstructable and how it became true is answerable. v2 fits that model with immutable events, judgments, and versioned interpretations.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 11 requires Foundry to answer why a meaningful artifact exists, what intent requires it, what evidence and verification support it, what depends on it, who authorized it, how it changed, and whether actual behavior diverges from intended behavior.
drafts.subject: Meaningful artifacts

drafts.rationale: Law 12 requires one universal lifecycle and semantic core across software, infrastructure, data, ML, agents, models, prompts, and future artifacts, with domain adapters not creating separate sources of truth.
drafts.subject: Foundry architecture

drafts.rationale: Law 13 states Foundry scales by decomposition, persistent state, and compiled context rather than one model holding the whole project, and that global understanding belongs to the system representation. v2 restates this as cluster-bounded reasoner inputs and Foundry-owned addresses.
drafts.subject: System understanding

drafts.rationale: Law 14 states that creation and operation are the same reconciliation loop at different lifecycle points and that the architecture must not split development and operations into unrelated control systems.
drafts.subject: Foundry lifecycle

drafts.rationale: Law 15 states that if a proposed implementation violates these laws for convenience the implementation must change, and that a law may be amended only explicitly with evidence and rationale preserved in history.
drafts.subject: Foundry Constitution

drafts.rationale: The v2 design document is marked PROPOSED, awaiting architect review, not approved, and not implemented, and it contains no implementation and no implementation plan.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The v2 design supersedes nothing and states that Intent Intelligence v1 remains frozen and unmodified, including in the smallest implementable slice.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1

drafts.rationale: The problem statement says v1 discovers the right unresolved issues then emits each one several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1

drafts.rationale: The design's organising rule is that AI understands meaning and Foundry governs meaning: AI alone may answer open-ended meaning questions as provenance-bearing proposals, and deterministic Foundry alone may admit, apply, or refuse state transitions and may never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The architectural thesis states that discovery output is disposable while interpreted, governed semantic state is durable, and that gaps and later architecture decisions are projected from that persistent state.
drafts.subject: Discovery output

drafts.rationale: Option A and Option B are rejected; Option C is recommended: keep v1 discovery framing, emit ephemeral semantic candidates, then retrieve, adjudicate, deterministically consolidate into persistent semantic state, classify late, and project gaps.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Section 4.4 forbids same subject string, same GapKind, high embedding similarity, shared source event, shared semantic ancestor, or AI confidence above a threshold from ever becoming an authoritative semantic rule; each may only decide what deserves comparison.
drafts.subject: Semantic equality

drafts.rationale: Section 7.1 assigns subject, facet, and scope to the address and predicate, value, and unit to the claim, because folding the asserted value into identity would make conflicting retention periods different things and destroy the conflict.
drafts.subject: Semantic primitive

drafts.rationale: A semantic address is identified by a Foundry-owned opaque address_id; subject, facet, and scope are descriptors never compared for equality, and a candidate reaches an address only through an admitted AI binding judgment.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: Consolidation is the deterministic application of admitted relationship judgments to yield one live issue per address by merging addresses, unioning evidence, and appending claims; claims are never merged, rewritten, or averaged, and duplicates are represented rather than deleted.
drafts.subject: Consolidation

drafts.rationale: GapKind is removed from identity entirely because none of 44 measured duplicate pairs shared a kind, and it is assigned by AI only after consolidation over the consolidated issue; discovery may emit only a non-binding gap hypothesis.
drafts.subject: GapKind

drafts.rationale: The design makes Gap a deterministic projection from persistent issues that are open, claimed, or disputed and material, not the durable object; the durable object is the issue at an address.
drafts.subject: Gap

drafts.rationale: Conflicts are a first-class DISPUTED state computed from admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH, never a merge outcome; no transition may reduce distinct claim values at an address, and only an authority event can settle a dispute while leaving losing claims readable.
drafts.subject: Semantic conflicts

drafts.rationale: Grounding is an AI entailment verdict of SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, or CONTRADICTED per cited event; a valid source ID is never accepted as proof of substantive grounding, which is the deterministic invariant both v1 safety incidents failed.
drafts.subject: Claim grounding

drafts.rationale: BUNDLES never merges; AI must return a SplitProposal whose units re-enter retrieval, and Foundry refuses any split whose unit evidence edges do not union-equal the parent edge set. Sentence and clause boundaries are never used as semantic seams.
drafts.subject: Bundled candidates

drafts.rationale: v2 treats v1's materiality failures as an input-compilation defect: assess_materiality receives the issue plus existing canonical decisions, authority records, supersession history, and closure state, and policy projects a gap only when the AI judgment says genuinely unresolved and materially affecting intent.
drafts.subject: Issue materiality

drafts.rationale: Correction is always append plus supersede, never destructive mutation; every merge retains contributing candidates and the evidence union so it is reversible, and superseded judgments remain readable with original inputs and provenance.
drafts.subject: Semantic judgments

drafts.rationale: The smallest implementable slice keeps frozen v1 discovery, then retrieval, bounded cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, late classification, and gap projection, in-memory for a single run with the full invariant set. It excludes cross-run persistence, supersession machinery, embedding retrieval, materiality-from-canonical-decisions, and human escalation.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2 slice 1

drafts.rationale: The primary testable claim is that a persistent AI-semantic plus deterministic-governance pipeline can preserve frontier-level critical intent coverage while producing cleaner, better-grounded, less redundant unresolved semantic state than one-shot frontier analysis on the same evidence. The lifecycle persistence claim is explicitly not yet to be asserted.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The open architecture question blocks which experiment v2 must pass to be considered validated: cleaner single-pass output versus the section 25 lifecycle experiment, depending on whether per-cycle discovery remains differentiating or is treated as commodity.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2 validation

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §19 specifies correction as always append plus supersede, with the superseded judgment remaining readable together with its original inputs and provenance.

value.text: append plus supersede; judgments remain immutable and readable, never destructively mutated

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §17 and decision 13 state that Gap is projected from consolidated issues and is not the durable object.

value.text: a projection from persistent semantic state, not a durable record; the durable object is the issue at an address

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 11 lists these explainability questions and treats an unexplained meaningful artifact as technical debt.

value.text: why it exists, what intent requires it, supporting evidence, verification, dependents, change impact, authorization, history, and whether actual behavior diverges from intended behavior

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §14 defines BUNDLES plus SplitProposal, the evidence-union invariant, and that seams are an AI judgment rather than syntactic boundaries.

value.text: an AI BUNDLES judgment with SplitProposal units; Foundry enforces evidence-union equality and does not use sentence or clause boundaries as seams

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §3, §9, and §12 state that EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation and that consolidation merges addresses while claims stay append-only.

value.text: addresses only, never claims

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 12 requires one kernel across domains and forbids domain adapters from creating separate sources of truth.

value.text: one universal lifecycle and semantic core across software, infrastructure, data systems, machine learning, AI agents, models, prompts, and future computational artifacts

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §5–§6 reject Options A and B for v2's first form and recommend Option C.

value.text: Option C hybrid: SemanticIssueCandidate discovery, governed semantic state, then gap projection

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §25 enumerates what slice 1 must contain and what is explicitly not in slice 1.

value.text: frozen v1 discovery, in-memory addresses and issues for a single run, the full invariant set, recorded judgments, and conflict preservation; excludes cross-run persistence, event-store integration, supersession machinery, embedding retrieval, materiality-from-canonical-decisions, and human escalation

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 7 requires this independence; EV-T1-02 §8 restates that confidence lives on judgments, authority on claims, and provenance on both.

value.text: confidence, authority, and provenance as independent attributes

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §7.2 states that address_id is the durable identity and that subject, facet, and scope are descriptors, never keys.

value.text: a Foundry-owned opaque address_id; subject, facet, and scope are descriptors never compared for equality as identity keys

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 states this as Foundry's purpose in the constitution preamble.

value.text: to convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 3 forbids models as canonical memory; EV-T1-02 applies that law so durable semantic state does not carry a model's vocabulary.

value.text: the canonical memory of a project; persistent state lives outside models

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 2 defines intended versus actual reconciliation and requires every operation to act on that delta.

value.text: Delta = Actual State minus Intended State; every operation must help explain, reduce, verify, or explicitly authorize this delta

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §4.4 lists these shortcuts as never allowed to become authoritative semantic rules, only as candidate-retrieval hints.

value.text: same subject string, same GapKind, high embedding similarity, shared source event, shared semantic ancestor, or AI confidence above a threshold equating to same meaning

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02's open architecture question states that which experiment v2 must pass to be considered validated is blocked pending the architect's conclusion about discovery.

value.text: blocked choice between a cleaner single-pass output experiment and the lifecycle experiment in section 25

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 4 states this executor order; EV-T1-02 §20 applies it to v2 routing stages.

value.text: 1. deterministic computation; 2. cheap model worker; 3. stronger model worker; 4. frontier reasoning; 5. human authority

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §23 states this as the primary testable claim, with operational preserve/improve/maintain criteria against a one-shot baseline.

value.text: A persistent AI-semantic plus deterministic-governance pipeline can preserve frontier-level critical intent coverage while producing a materially cleaner, better-grounded, less redundant unresolved semantic state than one-shot frontier analysis on the same evidence.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 1 states that no artifact is canonical merely because it exists and that a production behavior can be real and still wrong.

value.text: mere existence; evidence may support or challenge intent, but existence does not automatically create authority

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 13 places global understanding in the system representation; EV-T1-02 repeats that no single brain must hold the whole system.

value.text: the system representation, not a single model invocation

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §1 names this as v1's core defect after showing discovery recall matched the baseline while post-discovery emission produced redundancy.

value.text: absence of durable semantic identity and of a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission, not a lack of intelligence

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01's Founding Thesis states this contrast and that Foundry preserves decisions and manufactures artifacts.

value.text: Implementation artifacts are replaceable. Decisions are durable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 status states that Intent Intelligence v1 remains frozen and unmodified and that the v2 design supersedes nothing.

value.text: frozen and unmodified; v2 supersedes nothing

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 15 requires implementation to yield to the constitution and forbids silent falsification of laws.

value.text: implementation convenience; a violating implementation must change, and a law may be amended only explicitly with evidence and rationale preserved in history

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 10 requires reconstructable append-only history; EV-T1-02 §18 maps that onto immutable events, judgments, and versioned interpretations.

value.text: an append-only history of material events, claims, evidence, decisions, amendments, verification outcomes, and promotions so current state is reconstructable from history

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §7.1 redistributes the six fields so values are not folded into identity, which would destroy conflicts such as 7-year versus 10-year retention.

value.text: subject, facet, and scope to Address; predicate, value, and unit to Claim

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §15 specifies this compiled input set so materiality is judged against what is already decided, not isolated prose.

value.text: the issue with its claims and evidence, existing canonical decisions at or near the address, relevant authority records, supersession history, and current scope and closure state

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 5 forbids self-certification; EV-T1-02 applies it so AI may propose but never apply a semantic transition and disagreeing judges apply no transition.

value.text: be the sole authority for correctness of a proposal or artifact; generation and verification are separate concerns

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §12–§13 and invariant 4 make conflict collapse structurally impossible rather than merely policy-prevented.

value.text: structurally guaranteed: consolidation merges addresses and never claims, so conflicting values become DISPUTED and cannot be cleared by merge

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 6 defines ambiguity as a first-class defect and requires progressive precision without treating a written rule as automatically executable.

value.text: a first-class defect; Foundry must detect material ambiguity, distinguish missing from ambiguous from beyond-capability decisions, and increase precision only as far as required

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 Status states the design is proposed, awaiting architect review, not approved, and not implemented.

value.text: PROPOSED — awaiting architect review; not approved; not implemented

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §16 and invariant 12 define this verdict set and explicitly reject treating a valid source_event_id as substantive grounding.

value.text: SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, attributed per cited event; a valid source ID is never proof of grounding; INSUFFICIENT is cut

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 14 requires Foundry to build and operate the same system as one reconciliation loop.

value.text: the same reconciliation loop at different lifecycle points; development and operations must not be split into unrelated control systems

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 8 forbids research from mutating canonical intent; EV-T1-02 §18 makes that flow structural by separating judgment-recorded events from applied transitions.

value.text: canonical intent; required flow is Research to Evidence to Reasoning to Authorization to Canonical State

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §3 states the architectural thesis that discovery output is disposable while governed semantic state is durable.

value.text: disposable; interpreted, governed semantic state is durable

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §4.3 states this responsibility-boundary rule as the contract every later section must obey.

value.text: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but never apply one; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse a transition but never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §3, §17, and decision 12 remove GapKind from identity and assign it late, after consolidation.

value.text: removed from identity entirely and assigned by AI after consolidation over the consolidated issue

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 9 forbids silent disappearance of material unknowns; EV-T1-02 applies that law so disputed conflicts remain in state even when projection is gated by materiality.

value.text: disappear silently; a known bounded non-blocking uncertainty may travel with the system, while an uncontrolled material unknown must block affected downstream work
